title: Welding-bead crystallization builds germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers
idea: A seam weld's moving melt bead resolidifies as one grain; deposit each 3D-DRAM tier as amorphous silicon on oxide and scan a solid-state green laser line across it so the melt zone recrystallizes laterally from a seed via into the tier below, building single-crystal channels tier by tier.
why: Current 3D DRAM plans use Si/SiGe superlattices, exposing a germanium chokepoint (China export controls) and costly epitaxy; seeded laser crystallization needs only silane and a diode-pumped laser (no neon-buffered excimer) and avoids SiGe strain limits on tier count.

title: Move purity from the quartz to a sacrificial inner liner
idea: Rearrange where purity lives: make crucibles from ordinary non-Spruce-Pine fused silica and spray an inner barium-doped devitrifying coat plus CVD Si3N4 liner that crystallizes into a dense cristobalite skin in the first hour, so the melt only ever sees the engineered liner.
why: Breaks the >80% HPQ chokepoint by letting any 4N quartz source qualify; target crucible cost down ~40% and supply base widened to dozens of quarries.

title: Substitute remote-plasma radicals for hot phosphoric acid nitride removal
idea: Remove sacrificial SiN (and lateral recesses for stacked 3D DRAM) with downstream NF3/O2/N2 radicals tuned for >100:1 SiN:SiO2 selectivity, replacing 160 C phosphoric acid baths that need continuous DI water spiking and heavy rinses.
why: Hot phosphoric baths are water- and energy-hungry; dry isotropic etch cuts the step's water >10x and gives the atomic-scale recess control 3D DRAM tiers need.

title: Supercritical CO2 cleans and dries tall capacitor pillars without water
idea: Jump from wafer scale to pillar scale: capillary forces during water/IPA drying topple 70:1 pillars, which is why support lattices and extra films are added. Replace post-etch wet clean, rinse and dry with scCO2 plus chelating co-solvents, which have zero surface tension.
why: Cuts ultra-pure water per capacitor module ~30-50% and removes the collapse limit, allowing taller unsupported pillars for higher Cs.

title: Substitute solid-state 193 nm lasers for neon excimer lasers
idea: Generate 193 nm light with fiber-amplified 1 um lasers frequency-converted through LBO and CLBO stages, replacing the neon/fluorine gas fills of ArF excimer lasers that drive immersion scanners.
why: Removes the neon chokepoint (historically ~50% from Ukraine) and F2 gas handling; no gas-refill downtime and better wall-plug efficiency for the DUV layers that dominate DRAM mask counts.

title: Deuterium kinetic-isotope passivation trims the leakage tail at 400 C
idea: Effect: the kinetic isotope effect. Si-D bonds at access-transistor interfaces and STI corners desorb 10-50x slower than Si-H because the heavier isotope couples to Si phonons. A final 400 C high-pressure D2 anneal, or a deuterated SiN cap, keeps tail traps passivated, suppressing the trap-assisted tunneling that sets refresh.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): 2-4x longer tail retention halves refresh energy; deuterium comes from abundant water.

title: Woodworking glueless joinery: solder-free hybrid bonding for HBM stacks
idea: Fine joinery such as dovetails holds without nails or glue. Replace HBM's SnAg microbumps and molded underfill with direct Cu-Cu/SiCN hybrid bonds between core dies, keeping the standard HBM3E/HBM4 base-die PHY and JEDEC footprint.
why: Removes tin, silver and underfill polymer per stack, thins each layer so 16-high fits the same height, and improves heat removal ~20-30%, easing the HBM TSV tax (fact 6).

title: Substitute zinc-tin oxide for indium-gallium oxide in gain cells
idea: Build 2T gain cells with amorphous Zn-Sn-O (or Si-doped ZTO) channels by ALD, controlling oxygen vacancies with N2O plasma and Al2O3 capping to reach ~1e-19 A/um off-current.
why: Keeps the ultra-low-leakage, near-refresh-free benefit of oxide gain cells while removing indium (China-dominated refining) and gallium (China ~98%), the scarce elements in IGZO.

title: Gravure-cylinder nanoimprint rolls DRAM honeycomb arrays
idea: Gravure presses print magazines from an engraved rotating cylinder; build a nickel-sleeved cylinder carrying the capacitor and landing-pad honeycomb and roll it continuously across a UV-curable, fluorine-free resist on each wafer, phase-locked interferometrically so every rotation lands on the same array grid.
why: Replaces several ArF-immersion multipatterning or EUV exposures on the array's most repetitive layers with a tool costing ~1/20 of EUV, using no photomask blanks, no tin plasma and ~1/100 the electricity per layer.

title: Ion-beam ripple self-patterning writes wafer-wide nanoline arrays without masks
idea: Ideal: line arrays that appear by themselves under a flood beam. Closest: off-normal low-energy Ar+ sputtering of an a-Si or metal hard-mask film spontaneously forms Bradley-Harper ripples at 20-40 nm wavelength, phase-locked by a coarse pre-pattern; transfer them as wordline/bitline gratings and repeat rotated 90 degrees for the crossing grid.
why: 100x: pattern formation costs one broad-beam ion-source step (tens of $k tooling) instead of SAQP/EUV, cutting array patterning per layer >50x and enabling ~$0.1/GB in multi-tier stacks; trades long-range order and line-edge roughness.

title: Ceria-free, slurry-free planarization by photo-cured resin etch-back
idea: Box [any cell | any access | any sense | any | Si | spin-on self-leveling resin + UV-ozone conversion + uniform dry etch-back]: replace CeO2-slurry oxide CMP steps (STI, capacitor top, ILD) with a self-leveling photo-curable siloxane resin that is converted to SiO2 by UV-ozone and etched back 1:1 to the stop layer.
why: Cerium (rare earth, China-dominated refining) and water: removes 6-10 CMP steps per DRAM flow, together with their slurry waste and a large share of rinse UPW.

title: Aluminum-core wordlines for arrays built entirely at back-end temperatures
idea: Periodic-table walk, Al (13): when the cell array is made of oxide-channel transistors at <=400 C, wordlines no longer need to survive 1000 C, so use low-temperature CVD Al (dimethylaluminum hydride, fluorine-free) cores with a 2 nm TiN skin instead of W or Ru.
why: Eliminates W (~80% China) and WF6 from the array; bulk resistivity 2.7 vs 5.3 uOhm-cm allows ~2x longer wordlines and fewer drivers, shrinking periphery.

title: COCOM-embargoed engineer patterns DRAM without EUV using block copolymers
idea: Persona: an Eastern Bloc engineer denied Western lithography, who turns to chemistry. DUV immersion defines guide stripes. PS-b-PMMA, or high-chi PS-b-PDMS, block copolymers then self-assemble into 24 nm-pitch lines and holes that correct and multiply those stripes. This replaces the 5-7 EUV layers of a 1-beta-class DRAM with ArF plus directed self-assembly.
why: EUV comes from one supplier at ~$200M per tool. DSA uses commodity polymers and could cut litho capex per wafer start by ~40%.

title: Po the fab never heard of helium: batch-tool gas-free flow
idea: Po: 'the fab has never heard of helium.' Extracted: build the 180 nm DRAM flow around batch vertical furnaces (LPCVD poly, nitride, oxide), wet etches and low-power batch plasma tools whose wafers sit on boats or mechanical clamps needing no backside gas; use hydrogen or argon for any leak checks and purges.
why: Helium (Qatar supply offline): zero helium in the bill of materials; batch tools also cost far less per wafer-pass.

title: Euler-buckled silicon-nitride nanobeams store bits as snap-through states
idea: Effect: Euler buckling bistability. A PECVD SiN beam deposited at 300 C with built-in compressive stress buckles up or down, two states separated by a barrier much larger than kT. Electrostatic electrodes snap it through in ~10 ns (GHz-class stiffness at sub-um length), and capacitive sensing reads its position; tiers stack in BEOL.
why: Refresh and capacitor walls (no stored charge to leak), using only Si, N and Al; density comes from stacking tiers rather than from EUV.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers using anodized porous-silicon sacrificial layers
idea: Magnify tier count past the SiGe strain limit: grow alternating heavily boron-doped and lightly doped all-silicon epitaxy, then anodize only the p+ layers into porous silicon, which is oxidized or etched out as the sacrificial layer.
why: No germanium (China ~60%+ of refining) and no lattice mismatch, so 100+ tiers stack without relaxation, past the 26+ tier 3D break-even (fact 2).

title: Solar-grade silicon plus RAID coding tolerates leaky capacitorless cells
idea: Solar uses cheaper upgraded-metallurgical silicon, and RAID tolerates failing disks. Combine both: build capacitor-free floating-body or gain-cell arrays on 6N-7N wafers and absorb the fatter leakage tail with row-level erasure codes that rebuild expired bits instead of refreshing everything faster.
why: Siemens polysilicon purification (~50-60 kWh/kg) and 11N purity are energy and supply chokepoints. Tolerating impurity-driven tails could cut substrate energy and cost ~20-30%.

title: Hyperscale DIMM harvest: retired DDR4 dies reborn as CXL memory
idea: Industrial users with 30-year lines already buy reclaimed chips, and hyperscalers retire millions of DDR4 DIMMs every 4-5 years. An automated U.S. harvesting line tests retired DIMMs, bins them by retention and refresh margin, and mounts them behind CXL memory-expander controllers as a cheap far-memory tier.
why: Zero new wafers or chokepoint materials: ~10-20% of server DRAM demand could come from the installed base at a fraction of the cost per bit.

title: Hourglass: unseparated zircon hafnium-zirconium precursors for capacitor dielectrics
idea: Stimulus 'hourglass' (zircon sand runs through unsorted) -> DRAM dielectrics and ferroelectric HZO do not need Hf and Zr separated; HZO even wants them mixed. A 10-person team makes metal-amide precursors directly from crude ZrCl4/HfCl4 (natural ~2% Hf), blended to target ratio, skipping nuclear-grade solvent-extraction separation.
why: Hf/Zr separation is a few-plant chokepoint; skipping it cuts precursor metal cost and dependence while using U.S. mineral-sand zircon.

title: Photostructurable glass revived: laser-written trench capacitors inside the substrate
idea: Photostructurable glasses (Foturan, APEX) died in MEMS because UV exposure gave coarse, rough features. Femtosecond laser-induced deep etching (one pulse train modifies a line that then etches ~100x faster) writes ~1 um wide, 20-50 um deep trenches into plain alkali-free display glass; line them with ALD TiN/Al2O3-TiO2/TiN so every TFT cell sits over its own in-glass trench capacitor.
why: The substrate becomes the capacitor: no plasma high-AR etch (no C4F8/SF6), no Hf/Zr, and picofarad-scale charge budgets let tiny, weak TFTs work; trenches are direct-written, maskless.

title: Eliminate storing what can be recomputed: controller rematerialization engine
idea: The memory controller keeps a small recipe table for pages derivable from other data (activations from layer inputs, decompressed tensors, positional tables) and regenerates them in a near-memory MAC array on access instead of fetching them.
why: A 3 nm op costs ~0.1-1 pJ versus ~10-20 pJ per DRAM bit moved, >10x per avoided access, and 20-40% less DRAM capacity has to be bought.

title: Shuttered Gen-10 LCD fabs reborn as stacked oxide-TFT memory fabs
idea: Giant LCD fabs are closing (Sharp's Sakai panel line halted in 2024) because TV panels commoditized, stranding PECVD, sputter, stepper and wet lines. Convert one into a glass-memory fab: 3-6 stacked oxide-TFT gain-cell tiers per ~9 m2 Gen-10 sheet, singulated into memory slabs, with only the host interface on a small chiplet.
why: Capital: reuses a ~$5-10B sunk fab at cents on the dollar; no Cz silicon, quartz crucibles, helium-cooled chucks or EUV; ~10 GB/m2 per tier at 1.2 um gives ~300+ GB per sheet, competitive as a capacity tier if sub-um patterning lands.

title: MgB2 persistent-current loops cooled without helium
idea: Inverts 'superconducting memory needs liquid helium': store bits as persistent currents in MgB2 loops (Tc 39 K; magnesium and boron are abundant) switched by kinetic-inductance gates, cooled to ~20 K by neon- or hydrogen-cycle cryocoolers instead of helium.
why: Persistent currents never decay, so zero refresh and near-zero static power; sidesteps the helium chokepoint for cryogenic AI or quantum data centers.

title: Fixed-abrasive pad releases its own silica, ending ceria STI polish
idea: Combine pad and slurry: a polyurethane pad loaded with sol-gel silica nodules releases fresh colloidal silica as it is conditioned, while an amino-acid additive in plain water supplies the oxide/nitride selectivity ceria normally provides.
why: Removes cerium (China-dominated rare earth) from STI/ILD CMP and cuts slurry volume, water and waste ~70%.

title: Re-fuse spent crucible cullet into outer walls of new crucibles
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity, rebuilding crucibles from crucibles: crush spent devitrified CZ crucibles, acid-leach the silicon residue, and arc-fuse the cristobalite cullet into the structural outer layer of new crucibles. Only a 2-3 mm inner layer, the part that touches the melt, uses virgin Spruce Pine or synthetic quartz.
why: HPQ chokepoint (Spruce Pine >80%). The outer layer is ~70-80% of crucible mass, so virgin HPQ per crucible drops ~3-4x.

title: Rice farmer refines husk ash into crucible-grade silica
idea: Persona: a rice farmer whose husk ash is ~90% amorphous silica. Acid-leach the ash, then hot-chlorinate it at ~1200 C to volatilize alkali, Fe, Al and B as chlorides. Vacuum-fuse the purified powder into HPQ-substitute crucible sand, sourced from U.S. rice states (~1 Mt of husk per year).
why: Quartz chokepoint: an agricultural waste stream replaces Spruce Pine sand, if purity reaches <10 ppm metals.

title: Recover backgrinding swarf as feedstock-grade silicon
idea: Scale shift: a stacked DRAM die keeps 30-50 um of a 775 um wafer, so >93% of the silicon becomes sludge. Collect it unmixed from backgrind tools at existing OSATs, then centrifuge, acid-leach and remelt it as solar or carrier-grade feedstock.
why: Each HBM wafer discards ~120 g of silicon. Recovery cuts polysilicon demand and its ~50-70 kWh/kg energy for the carrier/solar loop.

title: Rice-husk biogenic silica feeds synthetic Czochralski crucibles
idea: Periodic-table walk, Si+O (14,8): acid-leach rice-husk ash (~90% amorphous SiO2) with HCl/citric acid, calcine it to high-purity silica, and slip-cast crucibles with an inner sol-gel synthetic-silica layer; U.S. rice states supply millions of tonnes of husk.
why: Breaks the >80% Spruce Pine high-purity-quartz chokepoint with a renewable domestic feedstock, purified without HF.

title: Zonal car memory pool shares one hot-rated DRAM bank
idea: Minify DRAM per vehicle: a zonal architecture puts one ECC-protected, 125 C-qualified DRAM pool in the central computer and serves zone controllers over PCIe or automotive Ethernet, instead of each ECU carrying its own.
why: Cuts DRAM per car ~30-40% and the count of Grade-1 parts, with fewer packages and less tungsten and hafnium per car.

title: Reclaim end-of-life solar silicon as purified DRAM polysilicon feed
idea: Box [feedstock: retired PV cells | purification: hydrochlorination to trichlorosilane | deposition: US Siemens reactors | product: 11N poly for CZ]: delaminate retired modules, strip Ag/Al from the 5-6N cells, convert the silicon to trichlorosilane and re-deposit electronic-grade polysilicon.
why: Polysilicon concentration and energy: PV waste reaches millions of tonnes in the 2030s; recycled feed skips carbothermic reduction and diversifies a China-heavy supply chain.

title: Thin-film iron flux rings: core memory reborn at nanoscale
idea: Inverts 'core memory is obsolete': pattern ~60 nm Fe-Si alloy nanorings that hold clockwise or counterclockwise flux-closure states, switch them by current through a central post, and read them by the voltage spike induced in a sense line on switching (destructive read with write-back), as ferrite cores did.
why: Nonvolatile, so zero refresh; magnetic switching does not wear; no tunnel barrier, MgO, Co, Pt or Ru, just Fe and Si.

title: Nanoimprint plus block-copolymer DSA prints DRAM arrays without excimer lasers
idea: Box [ZrO2 cap | buried-WL Si | voltage SA | standard | CZ Si | jet-and-flash NIL cured by 365 nm LEDs + PS-b-PMMA DSA annealed in N2 + O2/HBr/N2 transfer etch with no Ar dilution]: imprint guide patterns at 2x pitch from e-beam-written masters, then let the block copolymer split them into 12 nm honeycomb holes and lines.
why: Neon (ArF laser buffer gas) and EUV (whose CO2 drive laser runs on a helium mix): removes all array-layer excimer and EUV exposures; NIL tool capex is ~1/4 of EUV and power ~1/10.

title: Undercritical ferroelectric zinc-magnesium oxide adds negative-capacitance boost
idea: TRIZ #16 Partial action: place a thin wurtzite Zn1-xMgxO ferroelectric (a 2021 discovery made only of abundant elements) in series with Al2O3 and deliberately keep it just short of switching. It then operates in its negative-capacitance region and raises total stack capacitance above that of the Al2O3 alone.
why: Could boost Cs ~1.5-3x at the same geometry with only Zn, Mg, Al and O. The risks are negative-capacitance stability and leakage at ns timescales.

title: Turbo-generator hydrogen cooling replaces helium on wafer chucks
idea: Adapted from large power-plant turbo-generators, which are cooled with pressurized hydrogen because its thermal conductivity beats helium's. Feed electrolyzer-made H2 at ~5-15 Torr into the sealed e-chuck backside gap of deposition, implant and non-H-sensitive etch tools, with generator-style purity monitors, dilution exhaust below LEL and purge interlocks.
why: Removes the largest fab helium use (backside cooling). H2 conductivity ~0.18 W/mK vs He ~0.15, and it is made on site from water and power, so the supply is domestic and unlimited.

title: Bacterial S-layer protein crystals as honeycomb capacitor masks
idea: Worsen: require EUV scanners from one supplier, tin plasma and hydrogen to print every capacitor array. Flip: self-assemble bacterial surface-layer proteins, which naturally form 2D hexagonal crystals with 10-30 nm periods, on the wafer, mineralize them into an oxide hard mask, and use that lattice to set the capacitor honeycomb with one coarse DUV alignment layer.
why: EUV single-supplier dependency and litho capital (5-7 EUV layers): the proteins are grown in fermenters from sugar, and 1-2 EUV layers could go if defectivity is solved.

title: Boron cluster molecules for fluorine-free p-type doping
idea: Periodic-table walk, B (5): replace BF3/BF2+ implants with octadecaborane (B18H22) cluster implantation or monolayer doping from boronic-acid esters plus spike anneal, with no fluorine co-implant and no BF3 gas cabinets.
why: Removes a major fluorinated implant gas; cluster beams give ~10-20x effective low-energy dose rate, so fewer implanters.

title: All-perovskite SrTiO3 capacitors on SrMoO3 electrodes shrink lateral 3D cells
idea: In 3D DRAM the lateral capacitor sets cell length and capacitance per area scales with k, so SrTiO3 (k~150-300) shortens it ~5x versus ZrO2. Use lattice-matched SrMoO3 (~1.8% mismatch, ~5 uOhm-cm, the most conductive oxide) for both electrodes, with an oxygen-getter interlayer to stop insulating SrMoO4 forming.
why: 5x shorter lateral cell x 40 tiers = ~10x density at equal tier cost; removes Hf, Zr, Ru and W from the capacitor using Sr, Ti and Mo.

title: Supercritical CO2 dries capacitor pillars without collapse or water
idea: Combine final rinse/dry with mechanical protection (zero masks): after the mold strip, displace water with a co-solvent and then closed-loop supercritical CO2 (zero surface tension) so tall pillars never see capillary force.
why: Ends pillar collapse that caps aspect ratio, enabling AR ~100 for more charge and fewer SiN supporter layers, while cutting final-rinse UPW and IPA.

title: Optical-fiber preform chemistry builds synthetic crucible inner walls
idea: Optical-fiber preforms are made by flame-hydrolyzing SiCl4 (VAD/OVD) into ultra-pure soot that is sintered into glass. Deposit a 3-5 mm VAD-soot synthetic-silica inner layer onto a crucible shell made of ordinary non-Spruce-Pine quartz sand, then vacuum-sinter it bubble-free so the melt only ever touches synthetic silica.
why: Breaks the >80% Spruce Pine dependence by needing ultra-high purity only in a thin liner; SiCl4 is a by-product of polysilicon production. HPQ demand per crucible falls ~80%.

title: Eliminate helium and leakage: liquid-nitrogen-cooled DRAM at 0.4 V
idea: Immerse DRAM stacks in LN2 made on site from air (no helium), retarget access-transistor thresholds for 77 K, and run the array at 0.4-0.5 V, where copper resistance is ~6x lower and the leakage tail vanishes so refresh is dropped.
why: ~6x from V2, refresh removed and smaller drivers give ~10x at the memory; the 77 K plant overhead only pays off when shared with cryo-cooled logic pods.

title: Vapor-deposited zinc-imidazolate framework as a dry photoresist
idea: Periodic-table walk, Zn (30): grow ZIF-8-type zinc 2-methylimidazolate films by CVD/ALD; EUV or e-beam exposure changes linker bonding so films develop in vapor or non-fluorinated solvent, with no PFAS photoacid generator, no fluorinated surfactant and no spin-coat waste.
why: PFAS-free patterning; Zn has high EUV absorption (lower dose); eliminates the ~95% of spin-coated resist that is discarded.

title: Metal-free vertical-bitline 3D gain-cell stack with doped-polysilicon wordline tiers
idea: Bits rise linearly with tiers while wafer cost rises ~1% per tier because lithography is shared. Stack 120 tiers of in-situ-doped poly-Si wordlines (no W replacement gate) with 2T0C Zn-Sn-O gain cells around vertical bitline holes in a relaxed ~100x100 nm per-tier footprint; gain cells tolerate poly resistance because their gate load is ~0.1 fF.
why: ~85 nm2/bit effective vs 864 nm2 today = ~10x density; ~20% added deposition/etch cost is offset by deleting 5-7 EUV layers; zero W, In or Ga.

title: Eliminate hafnium, zirconium and ruthenium: rutile TiO2 templated on SnO2 electrodes
idea: Use conductive rutile SnO2 (oxygen-vacancy or F-doped) as the storage-node electrode; its rutile lattice templates ALD TiO2 from TiCl4 and water into the rutile phase at <=300 C, giving k~80-100, with a 0.5 nm Al2O3 interlayer to curb leakage.
why: Hits fact 1's k~70 target without Ru templates (~90% South Africa) or Hf/Zr precursors; ~1.5x Cs at the same aspect ratio, or capacitor AR cut from ~70:1 to ~45:1.

title: Substitute per-gigabit water allowances for volumetric fab water permits
idea: State permits and CHIPS-style grant terms meter fabs in liters per Gb shipped rather than total gallons, with a published ratchet to 10x lower within 8 years and tradable credits for fabs that beat the curve, funding dry-tool retrofits.
why: Makes water a per-step design target that pulls the dry technologies into production and lets more DRAM capacity fit in water-stressed US sites such as Arizona and Idaho.

title: Glass-lined, SiC-coated wet benches replace fluoropolymer plumbing
idea: Within $1M/24 months: build one acid wet-bench loop with borosilicate-glass-lined stainless piping, CVD-SiC tank linings and ceramic valve seats instead of PFA/PTFE, and qualify metal-ion leaching to ppt levels over 12 months.
why: Fabs depend on PFA/PTFE wetted parts that pending PFAS restrictions threaten; a proven fluoropolymer-free path de-risks every U.S. fab.

title: Mirror-polarity cells share every electrode between adjacent tiers
idea: A capacitor plate's field lines can terminate on both faces, yet stacked cells use only one; flip cell polarity on alternate tiers so one TiN/Mo plate serves the cells above and below as a common plate, deleting one metal layer per tier.
why: Tier height down ~30% and metal ALD per bit down ~50%: ~130 instead of 100 tiers per etchable height, which with a relaxed gain cell gives ~10x at equal cost.

title: 1970s molybdenum-gate MOS revived to replace tungsten wordlines
idea: Revive molybdenum-gate MOS, and the WWII practice of substituting molybdenum for tungsten: fill buried wordlines and bitline contacts with barrier-thin Mo deposited from MoCl5/MoO2Cl2 instead of WF6, sourced from US mines.
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%) and fluorine use (WF6): Mo's short electron mean free path lowers narrow-line resistance; claims near-zero tungsten per wafer.

title: 1970s molybdenum-gate MOSFETs revived as fluorine-free buried wordlines
idea: Mo-gate MOS of the 1970s was abandoned because molybdenum oxidized and etched badly next to polysilicon. A buried wordline entombs the metal: deposit Mo by ALD from MoO2Cl2 (chlorine, not fluorine) directly on a thin barrier, recess it, and seal it with SiN so oxidation never occurs.
why: Replaces TiN/W buried wordlines: Mo has lower narrow-line resistivity than W, the U.S. mines roughly a quarter of world Mo (Colorado) versus ~80% China for W, and WF6 is eliminated; ~20-30% lower wordline RC.

title: Hurricane-proof quartz: chlorination-upgraded vein quartz from five countries
idea: Hurricane Helene's 2024 shutdown of Spruce Pine is the extreme edge case: design crucible supply to survive it. Upgrade ordinary hydrothermal vein and pegmatite quartz (Norway, Brazil, India, Quebec, Arizona) by 1200 C Cl2/HCl gas leaching plus electrodiffusion 'sweeping', the field-driven alkali removal used for oscillator-grade quartz, to reach <10 ppm total impurities.
why: Second-sources the >80% single-region HPQ chokepoint through geographic diversity instead of reliance on one ore body.

title: Electroless nickel-boron plating fills contacts without WF6
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ni (28): activate silicided contact bottoms and plate Ni-B bottom-up from an aqueous NiSO4 plus dimethylamine-borane bath at 60-80 C with a suppressor additive, then anneal to form NiSi at the interface.
why: Replaces CVD tungsten (WF6, China W) for cell and periphery contacts with a low-capital wet bench; fluorine-free.

title: Coral electro-accretion: electrodeposited capacitor dielectric from water
idea: Biorock reefs grow mineral on a cathode straight from seawater. Generate base electrochemically at the TiN storage-node surface in an aqueous zirconyl/titanyl bath, so a conformal ZrO2-TiO2 film precipitates evenly down 70:1 holes and stops itself as it becomes insulating, then densify it with an anneal.
why: Self-limiting electro-accretion grows only on electrodes with near-100% precursor use, versus <10% for ALD metalorganics, and needs no hafnium.

title: MEMS parametrons store bits as oscillation phase, no leakage tail
idea: Revive Eiichi Goto's 1954 parametron with AlN-on-silicon micro-resonators pumped at twice their natural frequency. Each resonator settles into a 0 or pi phase state that persists as long as the shared pump runs, and is read by phase comparison with a reference line.
why: Retention depends on a shared resonant pump (Q~1e4), not on leakage, so the refresh tail disappears (fact 3); uses only Al, N and Si (no Hf, W or In); fits refresh-free scratchpads next to accelerators.

title: Molybdenum dioxide electrode replaces ruthenium and templates rutile TiO2
idea: Combine the capacitor bottom electrode with the dielectric's crystal seed: metallic, rutile-type ALD MoO2 plays the templating role RuO2 plays in lab stacks, nucleating rutile TiO2 (k ~80-100) at <=400 C, with an Al-doped TiO2 interface layer to cut leakage.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (needs k ~70) without ruthenium (South Africa ~85-90%); Mo is U.S.-mined; ~1.5-2x Cs at the same aspect ratio.

title: LNG regasification cold runs a 77 K refresh-free memory tier
idea: Effect: thermally activated junction and GIDL leakage collapse at 77 K, stretching DRAM retention from 64 ms to hours. Build cryo-memory pods at LNG import terminals, where regasification throws away ~830 kJ of cold per kg, and cool commodity DRAM with liquid-nitrogen loops (never helium) at re-centered voltages.
why: Refresh energy (16-33% of idle power) nearly eliminated, lower VARY possible, helium-free cryogenics, and wasted industrial cold reused as a power source.

title: Wurtzite ZnMgO ferroelectric capacitors replace hafnia and scandium
idea: Box [Zn0.6Mg0.4O ferroelectric polarization | Si access | charge sense with write-back | near-planar stacked cap | CZ Si | ALD/MOCVD]: use wurtzite zinc-magnesium oxide, whose ~80 uC/cm2 switchable polarization gives roughly 10x the signal charge of a 5 fF linear cap in a near-planar footprint.
why: Avoids Hf (HZO) and Sc (AlScN; scandium is China/Russia-dominated and very expensive); Zn and Mg are abundant and US-sourced, and a planar cell removes the high-AR etch; endurance is the open risk.

title: PCB-etchant electrolytic regeneration recycles persulfate cleaning chemistry on site
idea: PCB shops electrolytically regenerate spent cupric-chloride etchant instead of buying new. Adapt this to wafer cleaning: electrolyze spent sulfuric cleaning streams on boron-doped-diamond anodes to regenerate peroxydisulfuric acid as the oxidant in a closed loop at each wet bench.
why: Cuts sulfuric acid and H2O2 purchases ~70-90%, along with their trucking and waste. The diamond electrodes can be made domestically.

title: Xylem-sap capillary wicking fills contacts without tungsten CVD
idea: Plants lift sap up narrow, hydrophilic, slightly tapered xylem vessels by capillarity. Make periphery and BEOL plug holes slightly tapered and plasma-hydrophilic, spin on a Cu-Mn nanoparticle ink that wicks to the bottom, then sinter at ~400 C so the Mn forms its own MnSiOx barrier while the copper densifies.
why: Replaces W CVD from WF6 in plugs (tungsten ~80% China, fluorine chemistry) with spin-on and furnace steps on cheap tools.

title: MLCC-style strontium titanate nanolaminate stretches pillar capacitors past k=70
idea: MLCC makers ship trillions of titanate capacitors made from abundant Ba, Sr and Ti. Grow ALD SrTiO3/TiO2 nanolaminates (Sr cyclopentadienyl + TTIP, two-step crystallization) inside TiN-lined pillars in a university fab, with Al2O3 interface doping to tame leakage.
why: Fact 1 says k ~70 is needed; STO reaches k ~100-150 below 10 nm, enabling ~2x Cs or ~40% shorter pillars (less high-AR etch and PFC gas).

title: Waterless cleans: supercritical CO2 replaces ultrapure-water rinses
idea: Inverts 'cleaning means water': run post-etch residue removal, particle cleans and resist strip in supercritical CO2 with small co-solvent doses (alcohols, amine chelators), recompressing and recycling the CO2; near-zero surface tension also stops 70:1 capacitor pillars from collapsing during drying.
why: Cuts ultrapure-water use across DRAM's 100+ wet steps by an estimated 40-60% and removes pillar-collapse yield loss; feedstock can be captured industrial CO2.

title: Coffee grounds: centrifuge skid reclaims ceria from spent CMP slurry
idea: Stimulus 'coffee grounds' (re-brew the spent grounds) -> a 10-person team builds point-of-use skids that filter, decanter-centrifuge and ultrasonically re-classify ceria abrasive from CMP drain and return it as slurry blendstock.
why: Cuts rare-earth ceria use per DRAM wafer ~50-70% and slurry waste; complements abrasive substitution.

title: Antifreeze-protein mimics template high-k tetragonal zirconia without hafnium
idea: Antifreeze proteins bind specific ice crystal faces to steer growth. Dose face-selective small-molecule inhibitors between ZrO2 ALD cycles so they block the surface sites that favor the monoclinic phase, forcing pure tetragonal zirconia (k~40-45) without Hf or thick Al2O3 interlayers.
why: Raises effective k ~30% and drops hafnium from the capacitor stack, so the pillar aspect ratio could fall ~25% for the same charge.

title: Photonic curing: flash-lamp crystallizes zirconia in milliseconds, not furnace hours
idea: Plastic-substrate electronics that cannot exceed 150 C are cured with millisecond xenon flash lamps. Use flash-lamp annealing to crystallize ZrO2 into its high-k tetragonal phase and activate dopants in milliseconds instead of furnace anneals, tested on a university flash/RTA tool.
why: Furnaces are big energy and thermal-budget sinks: ms anneals cut anneal energy ~10x and can raise tetragonal fraction (higher k, more Cs).

title: Cavendish MEMS memory fixed: contactless bistable buckled nanobeams on glass
idea: Cavendish Kinetics' MEMS memory pivoted to RF because contacting cantilevers stuck and wore out. Make the bit the buckling direction of a pre-stressed, doubly clamped SiN or amorphous-carbon nanobeam that never touches anything: a coincident row/column electrostatic pulse snaps it through, and a sense electrode ~50 nm away reads it capacitively.
why: No transistor, no Hf/Zr dielectric and zero leakage in the cell, so no refresh; non-contact flexures survive >1e15 cycles; ~10-100 ns snap-through for ~1 um beams; built from sputtered films on glass.

title: Diamond-electrode loop regenerates sulfuric acid resist strip
idea: Within $1M/24 months: put a boron-doped-diamond electrolysis cell on the SPM resist-strip bath to oxidize spent sulfuric acid into peroxydisulfuric acid in situ, removing H2O2 dosing and recycling the acid instead of draining it.
why: SPM strips use large acid and peroxide volumes; closed-loop regeneration cuts ~80-90% of those chemical purchases and the wastewater neutralization load.

title: Smelter manager turns dead aluminum plants into memory fabs
idea: Persona: an aluminum smelter manager who knows where cheap firm power already lands. Site new DRAM fabs on shuttered U.S. smelter sites in the Pacific Northwest, Ohio Valley and Kentucky. These sites already have 300-600 MW grid interconnects, water rights, rail and industrial zoning.
why: Energy, water and time inputs: saves 1-2 years in the grid queue and ~$0.5-1B of infrastructure per fab.

title: Uni-Solar steel coils plus HP SAIL imprint for kilometer memory coils
idea: United Solar Ovonic (bankrupt 2012) ran roll-to-roll deposition on 2.5 km stainless coils, and HP's self-aligned imprint lithography encoded every mask level as heights in one 3D stamp with no overlay; both died on solar and display economics. Combine them: planarized, glass-insulated steel coil, oxide-TFT gain-cell memory deposited roll-to-roll, all levels patterned by one SAIL imprint roller and sequential etch-back.
why: Substrate ~$5-10/m2 versus >$1,000/m2 for silicon wafers; no Cz, quartz, helium chucks or EUV; one stamp replaces 4-6 masks; ~4 GB/m2 at 2 um, so cost wins only if processing stays under ~$15/m2.

title: Substitute carborane superacid anions for fluorinated photoacid generators
idea: Make photoacid generators whose anion is a chlorinated closo-carborane (CHB11Cl11-), a weakly coordinating superacid conjugate with no C-F bonds, giving PFAS-class acid strength and low acid diffusion in chemically amplified resists.
why: Removes PFAS (perfluoroalkyl sulfonate anions) from DRAM lithography without losing sensitivity or line-edge roughness, securing resist supply against PFAS bans.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal lengthens retention in existing furnaces
idea: Isotope-scale fix with a year-scale payoff: a final 10-20 atm D2 anneal in existing high-pressure furnaces passivates access-transistor interface and GIDL trap sites with Si-D bonds, which resist breaking and leak less than Si-H over the product's life.
why: Tightens the <=13 fA leakage tail. If retention doubles, refresh energy (16-33% of idle power) halves. Deuterium comes from abundant heavy water.

title: Coca-Cola bottler franchise for a portable capacitorless memory module
idea: Coca-Cola ships concentrate and lets local bottlers add abundant local water. Adapt this by licensing a capacitor-free BEOL memory concentrate (PDK, recipes, precursor specs, test IP) that any CMOS fab, including US 28-65 nm and MEMS fabs, bottles onto its own wafers with local, non-chokepoint materials.
why: Spreads memory supply across dozens of existing fabs with no new $15B fab. It uses only BEOL-temperature steps that are light on Hf, W and He, and could lift the US share well above 2%.

title: HDD glass platters inspire panel glass interposers for HBM
idea: Hard-disk makers moved platters from aluminum to ultra-flat glass. Replace the HBM silicon interposer (cut from 300 mm wafers) with a panel-processed glass interposer from the display/HDD glass supply chain, using laser-drilled through-glass vias and 2 um redistribution lines, while keeping the identical HBM3E/HBM4 PHY, microbump map and protocol.
why: Frees wafer-grade silicon and CZ/crucible capacity from interposers on top of the 3x wafer-area HBM tax; panels carry ~10x a wafer's area, cutting interposer cost ~40-60%.

title: Thin-kerf, thin-wafer diet: more wafers per crucible
idea: Imposed scarcity: ingot output frozen at today's crucible count. Slice 300 mm ingots with 35 um diamond wire into 450 um wafers (vs 775 um wafers with ~150 um kerf), and carry each thin wafer through FEOL on a reusable bonded glass or silicon handle that is debonded before backgrind.
why: Ingot consumed per wafer drops from ~925 um to ~490 um, so ~1.8x more wafers per ingot; the same Spruce Pine crucible and polysilicon supply feeds ~60-80% more DRAM wafers.

title: Substitute tin-catalyzed grown nanowires for etched storage pillars
idea: Grow vertical, heavily doped silicon nanowires by vapor-liquid-solid growth from tin catalyst dots (not gold, which kills carrier lifetime) placed on each storage-node contact, then coat with high-k and TiN to form capacitors bottom-up.
why: Additive growth reaches AR >150 with no high-AR fluorocarbon etch and no EUV hole layer; tin is abundant and electrically benign in silicon.

title: Hot-rated memory enables waterless dry-cooled datacenters
idea: Magnify the allowed memory temperature from 85 C to 125 C: qualify server DRAM to Grade 1 (temperature-tracking refresh, thicker capacitor dielectric) so racks can run 60 C warm-water loops with dry coolers and no evaporative cooling.
why: Saves ~1-2 L of water per kWh plus chiller energy, because memory no longer forces cold supply temperatures; a system-level resource lever.

title: Idle 65 nm back-end lines make interposers replacing glass-cloth substrates
idea: Scale shift from PCB laminate to wafer BEOL: existing 65-130 nm copper back-end lines pattern 2-4 metal-layer passive silicon interposers and bridges for DRAM packages and HBM-lite stacks. These replace BT/ABF laminates built on T-glass cloth.
why: Bypasses the T-glass/ABF substrate bottleneck and gives finer wiring for wider, lower-energy buses, using existing mature-fab capacity.

title: Run the fab to the sun: energy-time rearranged WIP
idea: Rearrange the time order of steps: hold larger WIP buffers before energy-hungry steps (EUV exposures, furnaces, anneals) so they batch into curtailed-renewable hours, while low-power steps run around the clock.
why: Fab electricity is a growing cost and siting limit; shifting ~30% of load to near-zero-price hours cuts energy cost ~20% and makes intermittent power usable.

title: Fluorine-free molybdenum buried wordlines from oxychloride ALD
idea: Periodic-table walk, Mo (42): deposit buried-channel wordlines by ALD Mo from MoO2Cl2 + H2 (chloride, no WF6); Mo's ~11 nm electron mean free path beats W's ~15.5 nm in 10 nm trenches, and without fluorine attacking the gate oxide the TiN barrier can be thinned or dropped.
why: Kills W (~80% China) and WF6; the U.S. is a top-two Mo producer (Colorado); ~20-30% lower wordline resistance.

title: Scribe-line sensors replace blanket monitor wafers
idea: Within $1M/24 months: put film-thickness, sheet-resistance and particle test structures in product scribe lines and pair them with tool-sensor virtual-metrology models, so process qualification uses product wafers instead of blanket monitor wafers; pilot with one fab partner.
why: Monitor and dummy wafers consume ~10-20% of prime-wafer starts; halving them frees silicon, crucibles and helium for real DRAM.

title: Gemstone-style cleaving recovers backside slabs from thinned memory wafers
idea: Stacked and HBM DRAM dies are ground from 775 um down to ~30-50 um, so >90% of the crystal becomes sludge. Adapt gemstone cleaving: after the front side is bonded to a carrier, an IR laser writes a buried damage plane ~60 um deep, and a thermal-stress pulse splits off a ~650 um slab that is repolished into a new wafer.
why: Each pulled wafer yields a second wafer, roughly halving crystal, quartz-crucible and energy per HBM bit. It also eliminates grinding sludge and grinding water.

title: Germanium recovered from Alaskan zinc concentrate and coal fly ash
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ge (32): recover Ge domestically from Red Dog zinc concentrates now shipped abroad and from Ge-rich fly ash via tannin precipitation and solvent extraction, dedicated to SiGe superlattices for 3D DRAM.
why: Removes export-control exposure for the SiGe sacrificial layers that 26+ tier 3D DRAM needs.

title: Robot-swappable chamber liners replace NF3 plasma cleans
idea: Worsen: clean deposition chambers by blasting NF3 plasma, a potent greenhouse gas, every few wafers. Flip: let films build up on a cassette of thin swappable aluminum or silicon liners that robots exchange in vacuum. The liners are stripped wet off-line and the recovered Zr/Hf/Ti oxides are refined.
why: NF3/fluorine use, GWP and tool uptime: liners are reused 50+ times and the metals in the deposits are recovered.

title: Robot-swapped recyclable aluminum chamber liners instead of NF3 cleans
idea: Periodic-table walk, Al (13): deposition chambers get thin anodized-Al liners that collect film deposits and are swapped through the load lock every N wafers, then remelted (secondary Al takes ~5% of primary energy) with residues separated as dross; sold as liner-as-a-service.
why: Eliminates NF3/fluorine in-situ cleans and their GWP; automated swaps keep uptime.

title: Move the wafer, not the gas: atmospheric spatial ALD
idea: Reverse which element moves: wafers travel under fixed precursor/purge gas heads at atmospheric pressure, instead of pulsing gases into a vacuum chamber around a static wafer.
why: Vacuum pumps are a large share of fab power; spatial ALD cuts pump energy and lifts precursor utilization (Hf/Zr/Ti amides) from ~10% to >50%.

title: Stage magician hides magnetism: Mn3Sn antiferromagnetic tunnel junction memory
idea: Persona: a magician whose magnet is invisible. Store bits in the chiral antiferromagnetic order of Mn3Sn and read them with a Mn3Sn/MgO/Mn3Sn all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junction. Write by spin-orbit torque in picoseconds.
why: Non-volatile, immune to stray fields, and roughly 2x denser packing. No Co, Pt, Ir or rare earths.

title: Eliminate indium and gallium: zinc-tin-silicon oxide channels for gain cells
idea: Replace IGZO with amorphous Zn-Sn-Si-O deposited by ALD or sputtering: Si binds oxygen and suppresses vacancies for a very low off-current, while Sn 5s orbitals carry ~15-20 cm2/Vs mobility, all from widely mined elements.
why: China holds ~98% of primary gallium under export controls and indium is a concentrated zinc by-product; this de-risks every oxide-semiconductor DRAM path at no loss in leakage.

title: Po transistors from solder metals: indium-gallium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cells
idea: Po: 'the transistor is made from melted solder.' Extracted: RF-sputter amorphous zinc-tin oxide channels for 2T gain cells patterned with i-line/KrF tools at <=350 C, replacing IGZO's indium and gallium (gallium refining ~98% Chinese) with abundant zinc and tin while keeping very low off-current.
why: Scarce-resource intensity for oxide-semiconductor memory; low-temperature gain-cell layers can be stacked over 180 nm CMOS to add density without new litho.

title: Indium- and gallium-free zinc oxynitride channels for gain cells
idea: Ideal: an oxide transistor built only from zinc, oxygen and nitrogen. Closest: sputtered or ALD amorphous ZnON (mobility 50-100 cm2/Vs) stabilized with a few % Si or Al to suppress anion vacancies, replacing IGZO in 2T0C and 3D gain cells while keeping wide-gap ultra-low off-current.
why: Removes China-concentrated indium and export-controlled gallium from the lead capacitor-less candidate; higher mobility than IGZO (~10-20) gives faster writes.

title: Eliminate long bitlines: 16-cell micro-bitlines over a hybrid-bonded sense layer
idea: Fabricate the cell-array wafer and a CMOS sense-amp wafer separately and hybrid-bond them at ~0.5 um pitch so every 16-cell bitline segment lands on its own sense amplifier below.
why: Bitline C drops from ~40-60 fF to ~3 fF, >10x lower activation energy, and Cs can shrink to ~1 fF, removing the 70:1 capacitor (facts 1 and 7).

title: HVDC thyristor valves shrunk into a capacitor-free bulk-silicon latch
idea: Grid HVDC valves hold state as latched pnpn thyristors that stay on at minimal holding current. Adapt a vertical pnpn thyristor per bit in plain bulk silicon, gated by the wordline to latch or unlatch, with a sub-uA hold current only on active rows and a slow-decay off state elsewhere.
why: Deletes the whole capacitor module: Zr/Hf ALD dielectric, TiN electrodes, nitride support lattice, and the 60:1 fluorocarbon etch with its helium-cooled chucks. That is ~20-30% fewer process steps and ~35% less PFC gas per wafer.

title: Wafer-scale memory slab with no package substrate
idea: Magnify the die to the whole wafer: redundancy-healed DRAM wafers bond directly to a logic wafer and a cold plate, eliminating dicing, ABF build-up substrates, solder balls and mold compound.
why: ABF film is a single-supplier chokepoint. Removes ~30% of module material and packaging cost and shortens wires (fact 5).

title: Po the chip is the whole wafer: 200 mm wafer-scale memory slab
idea: Po: 'one chip per wafer.' Extracted: on a fully depreciated 200 mm, 180 nm fab, pattern one wafer-scale DRAM with 4-8% redundant mats and 1990s laser-fuse rerouting, stitch a global bus with the stepper, and mount the slab with edge connectors; no dicing, bumping or packaging.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: depreciation (~55% of wafer cost) goes to ~0; ~6 GB per slab (8F2 cell ~0.26 um2, ~50% array efficiency) of cheap, domestic capacity-tier memory with packaging and test cost per bit far lower.

title: Panel-level fan-out packaging retires glass-cloth substrates for DRAM
idea: Scale jump from wafer to 600x600 mm panel: embed thinned DRAM dies in mold-compound panels and build redistribution layers directly on them. This removes BT/ABF laminates reinforced with T-glass cloth (one dominant supplier) and the gold or copper wire bonds.
why: Removes a 2025-26 substrate chokepoint, cuts package cost ~20-30% and gives thinner multi-die stacks.

title: Hot glue gun: PFAS-free laser-release adhesive for HBM thinning
idea: Stimulus 'hot glue gun' -> a 10-person chemical team formulates a polyimide/carbon-black laser-absorbing release layer and a hydrocarbon thermoplastic adhesive for temporary bonding during HBM wafer thinning, replacing fluoropolymer release layers.
why: Removes PFAS from HBM stacking flows; adhesive formulation is small-batch chemistry.

title: Po chips stamped like coins: nanoimprint for cell-array layers
idea: Po: 'memory is minted like coins.' Extracted: use step-and-repeat nanoimprint with replica templates for the highly regular cell-array layers (bitlines, storage-node contacts) and keep DUV for periphery; the imprint tool uses a small fraction of an EUV scanner's power and no tin or hydrogen plasma.
why: EUV capital (~$200M+ per scanner) and energy (~1 MW each) on array layers; template defectivity is the gate.

title: Steel minimill for silicon: remelt kerf and scrap wafers domestically
idea: Electric-arc minimills make new steel from scrap; build a U.S. silicon minimill that collects wire-saw kerf, broken and spent test wafers and off-spec ingot tops, acid-cleans and plasma-refines them, and directionally solidifies them into CZ recharge feedstock.
why: Kerf wastes ~40% of each crystal; recycling it reduces new polysilicon and its ~50-60 kWh/kg Siemens energy, giving a domestic loop independent of Chinese polysilicon.

title: On-site electrolytic hydrogen and nitrogen as the fab's only inerts
idea: Box [supply: PEM electrolyzers on reclaimed water + PSA N2 generators | uses: load-lock venting, carrier gas, PECVD dilution | leak test: 5% H2-in-N2 tracer with Pd-gate sniffers | storage: no rare-gas cylinders on site]: redesign the fab gas plant so N2 and H2 cover every inert role, and send the electrolytic O2 by-product to ozone generators.
why: Removes all He/Ne/Ar/Kr/Xe supply exposure for a DRAM fab using US-manufacturable equipment and renewable power.

title: Lithium-from-brine playbook: membrane skids harvest helium from U.S. gas streams
idea: Like Salton Sea direct-lithium-extraction plants that pull a minor element out of brine already being pumped, DRAM makers fund containerized hollow-fiber membrane plus pressure-swing-adsorption skids at U.S. nitrogen-rejection units, CO2 wells and small gas fields carrying 0.3-1% He, under fab offtake contracts that pay per liter delivered.
why: Turns dozens of stranded, sub-economic U.S. helium sources into a distributed domestic supply sized for fabs, so U.S. DRAM capacity no longer depends on Qatar or one large plant.

title: Substitute US wellhead membrane helium for Qatari LNG helium
idea: Deploy skid-mounted multistage membrane plus PSA units at US gas wells holding only 0.3-1% helium (too lean for cryogenic plants) and ship 99.999% helium in tube trailers on long-term contracts to fabs.
why: Replaces the offline Qatar ~30% share with distributed domestic supply; semiconductor demand is small relative to the reachable lean-well volume.

title: On-die microheater anneals heal aging access transistors in field
idea: Worsen: let BTI and hot-carrier damage pile up in access transistors until retention fails and the DIMM is scrapped. Flip: build in polysilicon microheaters, or use wordline Joule heating during scheduled maintenance windows, to anneal a bank locally at ~250-300 C and re-passivate traps, restoring the leakage tail.
why: Field life and refresh energy: repairs in place and could double service life, keeping bits in use longer.

title: Silicon double-barrier quantum-well memory: UltraRAM without indium or antimony
idea: Inverts 'nonvolatile memory must be slow and high-voltage': gate a floating node through a Si/SiO2/Si/SiO2 double barrier (two 1-2 nm oxides around a ~2 nm silicon well) that only conducts when a ~2.5 V write aligns the well level (resonant tunneling) and is opaque otherwise, giving ns writes and years of retention.
why: Zero refresh; elastic resonant transport avoids the hot-carrier oxide wear that limits flash; only Si and O, unlike InAs/AlSb UltraRAM.

title: Po energy is borrowed, never spent: resonant inductor wordline drivers
idea: Po: 'the memory borrows energy and gives it back.' Extracted: drive wordlines and bitline precharge from resonant LC tanks built with thick top-metal on-die inductors (easy in 180 nm aluminum processes), ramping lines slowly and returning their charge to the tank instead of dumping it to ground.
why: Voltage floor (CV2 stuck at ~1 V array and ~3 V wordline): 50-70% energy recovery on wordline and bitline swings; 180 nm thick-oxide devices handle the swings natively.

title: Redox-molecule monolayers store several-fold more charge in planar capacitors
idea: Ideal: a capacitor where every molecule holds electrons. Closest: self-assemble multi-state redox molecules (porphyrin/ferrocene tripods with phosphonate anchors, ZettaCore-style) on a TiN or doped-oxide electrode with an ionic-gel counter electrode; ~1e14 molecules/cm2 x 1-2 electrons gives ~16-32 uC/cm2 vs ~5-7 for a 1 V planar ZrO2 cap.
why: 100x enabler: lets cheap planar cells on panels/legacy fabs hold enough charge, collapsing the capacitor module (HAR etch, Zr/Hf ALD, several masks) into one dip-coat on the path to ~$0.1/GB. Trades molecule stability (needs >1e15 cycles) and redox speed.

title: Copper penny: copper-mine molybdenum precursor for tungsten-free wordlines
idea: Stimulus 'copper penny' (copper mines co-produce molybdenum) -> a 10-person chemical shop converts U.S. by-product MoO3 into ultra-pure MoO2Cl2 ALD precursor, enabling drop-in Mo buried wordlines and contacts without a TiN barrier.
why: Mo's shorter mean free path gives lower narrow-line resistance than W, and the U.S. is a top-3 producer; removes W and fluorine at the wordline.

title: Kintaro-ame candy draw: shrink a macro array into nanopillars
idea: Kintaro-ame candy hides a face in a log that is stretched and sliced. Build a centimeter-scale preform of glass, metal and semiconductor rods laid out as a DRAM capacitor and bitline cross-section, draw it ~10,000x on a fiber draw tower into a fused multi-core rod, then slice it perpendicular into dies whose pillars already have 100:1+ length, and bond them to a transistor wafer.
why: Forms high-aspect-ratio capacitor and contact columns with no EUV, no immersion multipatterning and no C4F6/C4F8 plasma etch (PFAS, high energy); one preform yields kilometers of identical pattern, cutting patterning capital and fluorinated gas per bit by orders of magnitude if registration can be solved.

title: Stressor-driven controlled spalling reuses one CZ wafer twenty times
idea: Effect: fracture mechanics. A tensile Ni stressor film plated at room temperature drives a crack parallel to the surface at a depth set by film stress (Suo-Hutchinson mode mixity), peeling 10-20 um single-crystal Si layers without kerf. Bond them to carriers at <=300 C for junctionless accumulation-mode cell transistors, re-polish the donor and repeat; sold as a wafer-leasing model.
why: Quartz crucible and polysilicon intensity per device layer fall ~10-20x, and every step stays at room temperature to 300 C.

title: Slip-cast synthetic-silica crucibles from polysilicon plant byproduct
idea: Potters slip-cast vessels from liquid clay; hydrolyze SiCl4 byproduct from a Michigan polysilicon plant into colloidal synthetic silica, slip-cast crucible bodies in porous molds, and arc-fuse them with a synthetic inner wall, all within one U.S. chemical park.
why: Turns a waste stream into crucibles ~10x purer than natural quartz, relieving the Spruce Pine concentration (a 2024 hurricane shut it) and foreign crucible makers; purer crucibles also cut oxygen-precipitate defects.
